uplift.envcat.title: Environment variables
uplift.envcat.intro: Expert knobs oMLX reads from the environment only — no settings.json field exists. Settable rows store the value in Uplift and seed it at server start; a variable already set in the launch environment always wins.
uplift.envcat.dead_hint: Not editable: no live oMLX code path reads this variable any more, so any value set here would do nothing. Documented so the name is not lost.
uplift.envcat.secret_hint: A credential or key. Uplift never edits it and masks its value wherever it appears.
uplift.envcat.set_hint: Currently set in the running oMLX process environment
uplift.envcat.stored_hint: Stored by Uplift, not yet in the process environment — apply it with the restart the badge above names
uplift.envcat.effect_hint: When a new value actually takes effect: immediately (oMLX reads it per request), on the next model load, or only after the server restarts
uplift.envcat.settable_hint: Editable here. Uplift stores the value and seeds it when the dev server starts; an unknown or wrong value can change engine behaviour, so it is labelled experimental.
uplift.envcat.managed_hint: Not editable: vanilla oMLX owns this variable. It either writes the value itself at runtime (a setting the dashboard already exposes drives it), or the variable is the environment fallback of an exposed setting — editing it here would conflict with that owner. Shown for reference only.
uplift.envcat.border_hint: Left border: this variable currently has a value in the running oMLX process
uplift.envcat.legend_border: coloured left border = currently set in the running server
uplift.envcat.intro_readonly: Reference only: this is the vanilla oMLX service. Uplift stores and seeds these overrides on omlx-dev only, so no value here can take effect on this server.
uplift.envcat.apply_hint: Apply this value now. Leave the field empty to reset: the stored override is deleted and oMLX returns to its stock default on the next restart.

uplift.voices.ref_text_ph: Transcript of the reference clip — exactly what is said in it.
uplift.voices.instruct_ph: e.g. Very happy. — tone, emotion, speaking rate in plain words
uplift.voices.instruct_title: Style instruction (Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice/VoiceDesign): natural-language control over tone, emotion and speaking rate. Empty = neutral.
uplift.voices.language_title: Force the output language, or Auto to let the model adapt to the text.
uplift.voices.speaker: Speaker
uplift.voices.speaker_title: Preset speaker of this CustomVoice model — no reference clip needed. Each speaker is strongest in its native language.
uplift.voices.sample_text: Hello! This is how I sound.
uplift.voices.transcribe_title: Transcribe the selected clip with a local speech-to-text model; check the result — the transcript must match the clip exactly.
uplift.voices.timeout: the server did not answer in {n}s — model load may be stuck; request abandoned (restart the server to clear it)
uplift.voices.edit_hint: Change the model to re-clone the SAME voice elsewhere, edit the transcript, or upload a new reference clip.
uplift.voices.saveas_hint: Saving creates a NEW voice with the same reference clip — nothing stored is modified.
uplift.voices.clip_keep: leave empty to keep the current clip
uplift.bench.help.accuracy: Share of questions where the model picked the correct option text.
uplift.bench.help.brier: Brier score: mean squared error between the probability the model states and the truth (0 = perfect). Lower is better.
uplift.bench.help.ece: Expected Calibration Error: the gap between stated confidence and actual hit rate, grouped into 10 probability buckets (0 = perfect). Lower is better.
uplift.bench.help.agreement: Position-bias check: the same question is asked twice with the options re-ordered. 1.0000 means the model picks the same answer text both times.
uplift.bench.help.ms_question: Average wall time per question (run time divided by samples). Each question runs several internal probes; see the ms/probe column in the exports.
uplift.bench.help.time: Total wall time of this benchmark run.
uplift.bench.help.samples: Number of questions scored in this run.
uplift.voices.prompt_title: Fills the transcript with a sample text for the selected language. Read it aloud while recording; edit it freely afterwards.
uplift.voices.record_done: Clip recorded — check the transcript before saving
uplift.voices.record_insecure: The browser only allows microphone capture on https or localhost — open the dashboard through a localhost tunnel, or upload a saved audio file.
uplift.voices.record_short: Only {n} s recorded — too short for a good clone
uplift.voices.record_title: Record a reference clip right here — read the suggested text aloud for 10-30 s in a quiet room.
uplift.voices.say_hint: Every voice this macOS offers. Installed voices speak instantly — no model to load; greyed rows need a download first in System Settings under Accessibility > Spoken Content > Voices. The button on a voice marks it preferred for its language; requests can also name a voice (say:<voice>) or a language (say:<locale>) explicitly.
uplift.voices.say_unsupported: The macOS say engine is not available on this server.
uplift.voices.say_nomatch: No macOS voice matches that filter.
uplift.voices.say_additional_hint: Installed on this Mac beyond the factory set — downloaded via System Settings.
uplift.voices.say_not_downloaded_hint: Not on this Mac yet — download it in System Settings under Accessibility > Spoken Content > Voices.
uplift.voices.say_count_hint: {n} speakable now, {t} offered for download by this macOS
uplift.voices.say_btn_chat: Make available for Uplift web chat
uplift.voices.say_btn_chat_hint: Speak chat replies with this macOS voice
uplift.voices.say_btn_chat_on_hint: Click to remove it from the chat voice list
uplift.voices.say_system_default: macOS default: {voice} ({locale}) — a preferred mark for this language overrides it too
uplift.voices.tts_hint: Every text-to-speech model installed on this server. Built-in voices come from the model's own metadata; your custom voices are grouped under their model. SETTINGS opens the same editor as in the model manager.
uplift.voices.tts_mac_stat_none: No overrides — every language speaks with its macOS default
uplift.voices.say_default_hint: The voice macOS already uses for {locale} — a preferred mark for this language replaces it.
uplift.voices.tts_none: No TTS model installed — download one in the model manager first.
uplift.voices.tts_set_default: Speak with this voice by default when a request names no voice
uplift.voices.tts_clear_default: Clear the default voice for this model
uplift.voices.tts_section_note: Used by every reading and voice output this dashboard produces with this model, unless the voice or the request says otherwise.
uplift.voices.editor_hint: EDIT closes this dialog and opens the voice in TTS & Voices, where its reference clip, transcript and settings live.
uplift.chat.cache_hint: Recorded reply audio lives with its message.
uplift.chat.cache_none: Audio cache: {files} files, {size}. Nothing to clean up.
uplift.chat.cache_confirm: Delete {orphan} orphaned audio files ({osize})? Replies that still have their message keep their audio.
uplift.gs.cc.desktop_hint: Expose claude-opus / claude-sonnet / claude-haiku as aliases of the tier models above
uplift.se.turboquant_kv_enabled.hint: Reduce KV cache memory using the selected format. TurboQuant supports 2 to 8 bits; Affine4 and Affine8 use 4-bit and 8-bit affine quantization.
uplift.chat.help_variants: Regenerate keeps every answer — switch with the tabs
uplift.chat.unsupported_files_skipped: Some attachments were skipped — unsupported file types.
uplift.dl.remove_task_tip: Remove this finished task from the list (files are kept)
uplift.gs.appearance.number_scale_hint: Per-browser display choice: compact rounds to higher units, exact shows every digit.
uplift.helper.launch_hint: Ready-to-paste commands (classic parity): env-prefix form points Claude Code at this server; the launch form loads the assistant with its assigned model.
uplift.se.pending.banner: PENDING RESTART — {n} saved setting(s) apply the next time the model reloads
uplift.se.rail.label: Sections
uplift.se.typenote.flip: The type override switches this form to the {type} family. The server rebuilds the engine with the override on the next load.
uplift.se.typenote.hidden: Generation settings (sampling, thinking, grammar, speculative decoding) do not apply to the {type} engine and are hidden here, exactly as in the classic dashboard.
uplift.se.typenote.sticky: Stored settings from the hidden families are NOT cleared by the type gate and keep their listed effect: {keys}.
uplift.se.typenote.template: Global templates can carry every setting; each model applies only the keys that fit its type.
